surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Philadelphia usually gets better looks than most teams, and Pittsburgh usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.5% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.9% against Pittsburgh) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

surprises.head: A shutout for Artūrs Šilovs
surprises.body: Šilovs stopped all 19 shots, worth 1.5 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 6 starts.

story.head: Šilovs shuts out the Flyers
paras: An ugly night for the Flyers. Nick Robertson made his Penguins debut, after six seasons with the Maple Leafs. Hendrix Lapierre made his Penguins debut, after four seasons with the Capitals. Robertson opened the scoring for the Penguins early in the first. The Flyers went 17 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the first to early in the second, while the Penguins put eight on net. Ville Koivunen made it 2-0 for the Penguins late in the first. The second was all Penguins: Evgeni Malkin scored on the power play, Lapierre scored, and Filip Hållander scored to make it 5-0. Robertson scored again shorthanded midway through the third to make it 6-0, and Egor Chinakhov made it 7-0 on the power play with less than four minutes left. Kaedan Korczak made his Penguins debut, after five seasons with the Golden Knights, and picked up two assists. Declan Carlile made his Penguins debut, after three seasons with the Lightning, and picked up an assist. Hållander finished with a goal and two assists.

No fluke here. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Penguins win about four in five. Artūrs Šilovs turned aside all 19 shots for the Pens, and Dan Vladař allowed seven goals on 38 shots. The Penguins moved to 1-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Flyers dropped to 0-1-0, still last in the NHL.
